title: Maine Property Condition Disclosure
description: Maine law (33 MRSA §173) requires sellers of residential real property to complete a property disclosure statement covering structural, mechanical, environmental, and other material conditions. The disclosure must be provided to the buyer before or at the time of the purchase and sale agreement.

required_actions.note: Exemptions: first sale of new construction, foreclosure, estate sales by personal representative who has not occupied the property.

title: Agency Disclosure — Brokerage Relationships
description: Maine requires real estate licensees to provide a written disclosure of brokerage relationships at the first substantive contact with a buyer or seller. 32 MRSA §13273 mandates this disclosure. Dual agency (called 'disclosed dual agency') is permitted only with informed written consent of all parties.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: In addition to federal lead paint disclosure requirements (42 USC §4852d), Maine has enhanced lead paint laws under 22 MRSA §1322-E. Sellers of pre-1978 residential property must provide the federal lead paint disclosure and pamphlet, plus Maine-specific lead hazard information. Maine's Lead Poisoning Control Act imposes additional landlord obligations.

required_actions.note: Provide Maine-specific lead hazard information in addition to federal pamphlet.

title: Radon Disclosure
description: Maine requires radon disclosure in residential real estate transactions. 22 MRSA §777 establishes Maine's radon registration and disclosure program. Sellers must disclose known radon test results and any radon mitigation measures. The Maine CDC recommends radon testing for all homes.

required_actions.note: Provide EPA radon pamphlet. Disclose any known test results or mitigation systems.

title: Closing Type — Attorney State
description: Maine is an attorney state for real estate closings. The Maine Bar Association's opinion and practice standards require that an attorney supervise the closing of real estate transactions. Title examination, document preparation, and settlement are considered the practice of law in Maine.

required_actions.note: Maine requires attorney involvement in closing. Attorney must supervise title examination, document preparation, and settlement proceedings.
